Title: Prisons Dept: Najib had health check-up, counselling besides Friday prayers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak did not just perform Friday prayers when brought out of his home in Jalan Langgak Duta where he is carrying out his house arrest.'
The Prisons Department said the former prime minister also attended to several other matters between 10.25am and 6.25pm.
It said Najib was first taken to Kuala Lumpur Hospital for a orthopaedic follow-up check, before performing Friday prayers in Kajang Prison.
This was followed by Quran classes at the prison and a counselling session with the prison's psychology officer.
"Once these matters were completed, (Najib) left the prison about 5.50pm and arrived at his residence in Jalan Langgak Duta about 6.25pm," the department said in a statement.
It said all Najib's movements were carried out based on established arrangements and requirements and were subject to standard operating procedures and house arrest conditions, under the department's supervision.
"The implementation of religious activities, healthcare treatment, rehabilitation programmes and intervention initiatives are among the aspects given due attention in the management of an individual serving a sentence," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar, Fahmi extend condolences over Zahidi's death
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the family of former deputy communications and multimedia minister Datuk Zahidi Zainul Abidin, who died today.
In a Facebook post tonight, Anwar prayed that Allah would forgive Zahidi's sins and bless his soul with mercy.
"May his family be given strength and patience as they face this great loss," he said.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil also expressed his condolences over the death of Zahidi, who was also a former Padang Besar member of parliament.
"On behalf of everyone at the Communications Ministry, I extend my condolences to the deceased's family and friends.
"May they be given strength, patience and fortitude in facing this loss," he said.
Fahmi also called on the public to pray for Zahidi, asking that Allah bless his soul, forgive his sins and place him among the faithful.
Zahidi, 65, was buried at the Bayan Lepas Cemetery in Penang after Isyak prayers. -- BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia's upper house to pick new vice president on December 2
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's upper house of parliament will pick the country's new vice president on Dec 2, its speaker said on Friday, after the dramatic resignation of Gibran Rakabuming Raka, the president's deputy and the son of his predecessor.
Gibran's resignation this week, which analysts say could widen the gulf between President Prabowo Subianto and former president Joko Widodo, followed a month of increasing political pressure from lawmakers after Indonesia's top courts ruled that he had inadequate education credentials to run for the job.
Speaker Ahmad Muzani said the upper house, which is tasked by law with appointing the new vice president, would now send a letter to Prabowo requesting that he submit two names for the job.
The house has also formed a team of 36 lawmakers to verify the candidates' credentials, Muzani said. It was not immediately clear which names Prabowo would submit.
On Thursday, Gibran said his resignation was a personal decision and unrelated to issues pertaining to his education credentials.
POLITICAL TURBULENCE
Gibran, 39, was elected alongside Prabowo in the 2024 election. Critics accused his father, Widodo, better known as Jokowi, of meddling in the process by influencing a court decision that changed the election rules, enabling Gibran to stand.
Analysts believe Gibran's resignation could stoke further political turbulence and lock Jokowi and Prabowo into a bitter rivalry.
Jokowi defeated Prabowo in two presidential elections, in 2014 and 2019. During Jokowi's second term, he made Prabowo his defence minister and tacitly supported the latter's 2024 presidential run.
On Thursday, however, both Jokowi and Gibran struck a conciliatory tone and said they would continue to support Prabowo.
Gibran, in a video address to volunteers shown by news channel Kompas TV, said he would not be in opposition even as an outsider to Prabowo's administration.
"I only have one message: Please, inside or outside government, we still have to support the president," he said.
Analysts said another sign of the gulf between Prabowo and Jokowi was last week's police revelation of an inquiry into suspected illegal wiretapping by four senior police officials, including former police chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo, who is widely seen as a Jokowi loyalist.
Police said on Thursday they had enough initial evidence to pursue treason charges against the four suspects for wiretapping Prabowo, other politicians, activists and journalists.
Reuters has been unable to reach the suspects for comment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman found strangled at home in Banting
Article:

Title: Vance trying to build own 2028 brand after midterm rout
Article:
Late in his blitz to salvage Republicans' midterm fortunes, United States Vice-President JD Vance has shifted strategy. He talked less about President Donald Trump and more about the issues that define his own political identity.
Vance argued the case for Republicans, who lost control of Congress, almost exclusively through the lens of his policy portfolio, according to a Reuters review of half a dozen speeches since the Republican convention in September.
He bypassed Trump's signature policies, including the Iran war and deportations, as polls showed the president's sagging popularity dragging down Republican office-seekers.
The change was deliberate, according to two people familiar with the strategy.
Vance and his advisers saw the issues he championed — economic nationalism, foreign policy restraint and public safety — as politically potent subjects he could address with authority.
The shift offered an early glimpse of how the 42-year-old vice-president could chart his own course as Republicans begin looking beyond Trump.
Vance hasn't said whether he will run for president in 2028, and Trump hasn't endorsed him or anyone else.
But Vance is viewed as a leading potential contender who some Republican officials say will need to inherit much of Trump's coalition while separating himself from his boss' baggage.
Vance took a more public step towards reinforcing his own political brand with an unusually blunt election post-mortem.
In a social media post, he blamed the Iran war for Republicans' midterm defeat and laid out a platform for a party rebound.
He called for a swift end to the conflict and urged Republicans to focus on affordability, reevaluate foreign relations and overhaul the US relationship with Israel.
Trump has called Americans' affordability concerns a Democratic "hoax". He launched a war against Iran following sustained lobbying from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Trump went on to endorse Netanyahu in the Israeli election.
The post for the first time put Vance openly on the side of ending the war.
Three people familiar with the White House and Vance's communications said the vice-president was not breaking with Trump and that White House chief of staff Susie Wiles knew in advance about Vance's post.
Donald Trump Jr., the president's eldest son, endorsed Vance's remarks on social media, along with some conservative allies.
The dialogue further elevated Vance as a potential post-Trump conservative standard-bearer, said Michael Ricci, a Republican strategist and former adviser to House speakers John Boehner and Paul Ryan.
He said Vance's message forced conservatives to debate the merits of the war, and more broadly, what core tenets Republican presidential candidates should embrace in 2028.
"This is about him using his megaphone of the vice-presidency to set the terms of debate," Ricci said.
White House representatives referred Reuters to Trump's comments last week, when he told reporters he understood Vance's perspective on the election results.
Democrats are poised to tie Vance —or any Republican nominee — to Trump in 2028, especially if Trump plays a large role in vetting conservative hopefuls.
"There's a real challenge of how you position yourself to be viable in a general election while winning a primary that still requires you to bow down and kiss the ring," said Igor Volsky, a Democratic strategist.
Vance's brand did not emerge from the midterms unscathed.
Republicans lost in states where he campaigned.
Some of the strategies he endorsed —including an ad by Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy that cast doubt on the sexual abuse suffered by the victorious Democratic candidate, Amy Acton — may have swung races away from Republicans.
Other possible 2028 presidential contenders have offered their diagnoses of the midterm defeat.
US Senator Ted Cruz of Texas said Republicans hadn't done enough on affordability.
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said losing candidates had focused too heavily on transgender issues and neglected voter concerns about data centres and artificial intelligence.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio has stayed silent.
Vance's effort to shape the debate was visible during the closing days of the campaign.
In stump speeches, he told voters to support Republicans because they would investigate fraud in federal healthcare and anti-poverty programmes, tying that to the White House's immigration agenda and cost of living.
He almost entirely ignored the Iran war and gas prices, and seldom mentioned Trump by name.
The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former Padang Besar MP Zahidi Zainul Abidin dies
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Padang Besar member of parliament Datuk Zahidi Zainul Abidin has died at the age of 65.
The news was announced by Arau MP Datuk Seri Dr Shahidan Kassim in a Facebook post tonight.
Shahidan described Zahidi's death as a great loss.
"I am deeply saddened to receive the news of my friend's passing. May Allah SWT forgive all the sins of the late Zahidi, shower His blessings upon his soul and place him among those who believe and do good deeds.
"To the entire family, may you be blessed with strength, perseverance and patience in the face of this loss," he said.
Zahidi served as deputy communications and multimedia minister from March 10, 2020, to Aug 16, 2021 and was also the former Padang Besar Umno division chief.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTviral: Amma is on fire with Silambam moves at Deepavali gathering
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An elderly woman has charmed social media users with an impromptu fire dance,
showing off her Silambam skills
with a flaming staff.
Spinning the long staff, with flames burning at both ends, she creates sweeping arcs of fire.
The performance took place at her family home in Batu Gajah, Perak, on Deepavali night. The video was posted on Threads yesterday by user gesh_de_wanderer, whose real name is L. Kunesegaran.
Kunesegaran said he had encouraged his mother to join them as they played with firecrackers during the gathering.
"While we were playing with firecrackers, my aunties and Amma were watching us. I kept insisting that Amma join us, but she was initially shy because around 16 family members had gathered at our kampung house, watching from the car porch.
"Eventually, I managed to convince her. To our surprise, she suddenly started showing off her Silambam moves!" he said.
He said he only learnt about his mother's martial arts background after the performance.
"Only after everything was over did she reveal that she used to be a Silambam player back in school," he said.
The video drew affectionate reactions from users, with many celebrating the reminder that mothers, too, were once young and had their own talents and playful sides.
"Sometimes we forget, our mom was also once a child," user anis.azziyati wrote.
"For a moment, I thought it was AI. So lovely to watch her in action," user numu.life commented.
Another user recognised her martial arts skills, writing: "Looks like she knew silambam."
"Amma is on fire!! Too cute!!!" user revera_rebels commented.
Silambam is a traditional Indian martial art believed to date back more than 5,000 years. Originating in Tamil Nadu, southern India, it uses a bamboo or wooden staff as its main weapon, with practitioners performing intricate spins and strikes that require flexibility and coordination.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AI firms court ex-spies as Nvidia crisis sets off alarm bells
Article:
ARTIFICIAL intelligence firms are hiring former intelligence operatives to help shield them from espionage, a risk thrust into the spotlight as Nvidia axed its chief executive officer, Jensen Huang, following reports of two extramarital affairs—one with an alleged Chinese spy.
Former intelligence officers, recruiters and company insiders say chip, AI and tech firms — which have boomed in the last few years on huge AI demand—have been beefing up their security muscle.
"The AI firms have snapped up a lot of security talent," said Christopher Falkenberg, a former US Secret Service agent and now Insite Risk Management president. "There are some very sophisticated people out of government thinking about security for these businesses... Demand outstrips the supply of people with relevant experience."
Revelio Labs, which tracks hiring trends, said counterintelligence hiring was a new phenomenon at frontier AI firms, with more explicit roles being posted in the last couple of years by the likes of OpenAI, Anthropic and Nvidia.
Most salaries ranged from US$200,000 up to around US$500,000.
Catherine Marinis-Yaqub, a former Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) officer who works for strategic risk and security firm Control Risks, said companies valued counterintelligence experts for their ability to spot threats, such as employees stealing trade secrets and attempts to exploit vulnerabilities, including via executives, by blackmail or coercion.
She helps executives spot threats that can look like chance encounters at gyms or coffee shops, which could be spies trying to befriend, blackmail or recruit them.
"They're just becoming more aware of it. They still have a long way to go."
The AI companies have brought in some big guns. OpenAI appointed former National Security Agency (NSA) director Paul Nakasone to its board and safety and security committee in June 2024.
It is now hiring a senior global security investigator. The ad lists counterintelligence as a key skill.
OpenAI fired an engineer last month after finding a recording device hidden behind a television in an executive conference room. The engineer accused of planting it pleaded not guilty on Nov 6 to illegally intercepting communications.
Rival Anthropic added former CIA deputy director David Cohen and former NSA cybersecurity director Dave Luber to the national security advisory council it launched in August last year.
Anthropic is seeking a threat-intelligence security engineer to track sophisticated adversaries. Its advertisement describes the company as "one of the most interesting targets in the world for nation-state and advanced criminal actors".
The pay, well above the public sector, reflects the relative scarcity of talent, said Kathy Lavinder, founder of specialist recruiter SI Placement.
She said top corporate security chiefs can earn US$1 million to US$4 million a year, depending on stock awards.
ASML, Europe's most valuable listed company, has built up its defences as its chip-printing technology has become a prize in the United States-China tech rivalry.
In the last few years, it has set up an Intelligence Fusion Centre and is currently advertising for an intelligence officer based in Taiwan, where ASML's top customer TSMC makes chips for Nvidia.
The ad reads like a job for a character from a John le Carré spy novel, tasked with rooting out "insider threats", including espionage, sabotage and terrorism.
Applicants need at least 10 years of counterintelligence experience.
Former ASML security chief Aernout Reijmer, who left the firm in September last year and now heads cybersecurity collaboration business CyberAlloy, said security chiefs' top priority has been the need to counter AI-driven hacking and the need to protect data as their own firms adopt AI.
That can leave less time —and less focus from boardrooms—to consider the risk of an executive falling prey to a spy, which at times is dismissed as far-fetched.
"I know many companies, I'd say 90 per cent, completely ignore that risk, because the James Bond theme starts playing in people's heads straight away."
He said the biggest tech firms and banks usually have decent defences in place, with big AI firms now obvious targets given the global "geopolitical race".
Lavinder, the recruiter, added that even a well-staffed team cannot always avoid issues or dictate the boss's private life.
"Security teams don't have a veto," she said.
"Executives will do what executives want to do."
The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar urges Melaka voters to reject exploiters of religion, corrupt people
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged the people of Melaka to use their ballots in the state election tomorrow to reject those who exploit religion for political gain, as well as individuals involved in corruption.
In a Facebook post tonight, the Pakatan Harapan chairman said Melaka voters had an opportunity to send a strong message and become a beacon of hope for those who wanted to see the country free from corruption.
"Over the past few days, we have witnessed the true face of a so-called 'unity'. For the sake of votes and power, they have stooped so low as to exploit religion by issuing fatwas legitimising support for corrupt individuals, demonising their opponents and even equating the choice of who to vote for with the obligation to perform ablution.
"Tomorrow, the people of Melaka have an opportunity to send a strong message through the ballot box. Reject those who exploit religion and those who hide behind the guise of championing the interests of the community but, in reality, are glorifying corrupt individuals," he said.
Anwar said the attitude of remaining silent and tolerating corruption had damaged the country for far too long and must be brought to an end through the voters' choices.
"We must put an end to it at the ballot box tomorrow. Save Melaka. Save the country. Vote for Harapan," he said.
A total of 675,166 voters are eligible to cast their ballots in the 16th Melaka State Election, with voter turnout expected to reach 70 per cent.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: Police put life and limb on the line to keep us safe
Article:
The police force is what keeps our homes, streets and country safe, something we often give little credit to in a generally peaceful Malaysia.
Theirs is a noble calling and we also tend to take that for granted, until an isolated incident  highlights that our policemen put life and limb on the line every day to safeguard what we all hold dear.
The recent heinous attack on a policeman in Kepong, which resulted in his hand being severed by a parang-wielding assailant, is a stark reminder of the risks and dangers that police personnel face in the line of duty. Much of the public discourse surrounding policing tends to focus on misconduct, abuse of power, corruption and shortcomings in law enforcement — and such cases must certainly be singled out.
Accountability and appreciation for the police are definitely not mutually exclusive. Police misconduct must be addressed but for every single act of impropriety, there are tens of thousands of upright uniformed men and women who quietly go about their work and take the occupational risks in stride.
We cannot honour them enough,  more so when general peace and safety reign throughout this land.
In holding the police accountable, however, we must not lose sight of the risks that come with the job, nor the sacrifices borne by those who wear the uniform.
For an officer responding to a report of a disturbance, domestic dispute or a violent individual running amok, there is often little time to assess the danger. What may appear to be a routine call can turn into a life-threatening confrontation within seconds.
The Kepong incident illustrates how high the stakes can be. It is fortunate that we have strict laws — such as on gun ownership — that help to keep both civilians and police personnel out of harm's way.
Still, the Kuala Lumpur police chief's reminder for personnel to remain vigilant and respond decisively is timely. The police force must ensure its personnel are well trained, equipped and supported, and recognised by the public for the risks they undertake on our  behalf.
Public appreciation for the police should not be confined to when they perform heroic acts of rescue or dramatic thwarting of crimes.
Their everyday exposure to danger deserves to be valued as a matter of course. The government and police leadership must keep ensuring officers receive proper protection, training, equipment and support, including medical and psychological care when they get injured in service.
Such police aid must also be regularly updated as new technology and methods become available. The public, too, must play its role. Respect lawful instructions, cooperate fully with investigating officers and avoid obstructing police personnel as they carry out their duties.
Above all, we must collectively ensure that the unfortunate case of the policeman losing his hand in Kepong — since reattached after surgery, thankfully — is an  isolated incident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar receives 11 outstanding underprivileged pupils from Kinabatangan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today received a visit from 11 outstanding underprivileged pupils from SK Singgah Manis in Kinabatangan, Sabah, accompanied by seven of their teachers, at Kompleks Seri Perdana.
In a Facebook post, the prime minister said he was impressed by the perseverance of the pupils and teachers, who had achieved various successes at state, national and international levels despite coming from a rural school.
"I advised the children to remain diligent in their pursuit of knowledge and to have the courage to chase their dreams. When they achieve success, remember to help their parents and give back to the community," he said.
Anwar also expressed his appreciation to the school's teachers for their commitment to educating, guiding and instilling confidence in the pupils to reach greater heights.
"The achievements of SK Singgah Manis pupils strengthen our resolve to ensure that every child, regardless of how far away they live, has equal opportunities to learn, develop their talents and achieve their aspirations," he said.

Title: Melaka election traffic builds up on Plus highway
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Motorists heading to Melaka for Saturday's election faced traffic congestion on southbound highways, with delays reported from Sungai Besi.
The Malaysian Highway Authority traffic hotline reported a build-up of traffic between Sungai Besi and Bangi from around 7pm.
A video shared by Threads user wallawaniey showed vehicles moving slowly along the Plus highway, prompting speculation that the traffic jams was linked to the election.
"It feels like the festive season rush. Is this because of tomorrow's Melaka election?" the user wrote.
Other users expressed surprise at the congestion, with one questioning why traffic was already heavy again after similar delays the previous week.
Another user said bus tickets from Kuala Lumpur to Melaka had sold out, suggesting a rush of voters returning home for the election.
Motorists were also advised to plan their journeys as southbound traffic could worsen with people heading to Melaka to vote and others travelling to Port Dickson for an RXZ gathering, which runs from today until Nov 15.
Voters in Melaka will head to the polls tomorrow, with 687,697 registered voters eligible to cast their ballots at 240 polling stations across the state.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: More than RM36m allocated for flood mitigation in Selangor 2027 Budget, MB says
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Selangor's 2027 Budget has allocated RM36.45 million for 47 flood mitigation projects under the Drainage and Irrigation Department.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the allocation would fund 30 ongoing projects and 17 new projects under the Second Selangor Plan (RS-2).
Of the 30 ongoing projects, 13 have been completed and are undergoing final accounting, nine are still being completed, two are at the pre-tender stage and six are at the design stage.
He said the Anak Sungai Damansara flood mitigation project in Petaling was completed this year, while 11 projects were in the process of appointing consultants and five remained at the planning stage.
"Of the overall allocation, RM9.15 million is for the Klang River Basin and RM7.35 million for the Langat River Basin.
"The allocation also covers the Sungai Buloh, Selangor, Bernam and Kapar Besar river basins, as well as preparatory works such as design, surveying and land matters.
"Our priority is to expedite projects that are ready for implementation and settle land matters and coordination early for projects in the pipeline," he said when tabling the RM3.3 billion 2027 Budget at the state legislative assembly today.
Amirudin said flood mitigation systems could only function effectively if local drainage networks were capable of channeling water into rivers with sufficient capacity to receive the flow.
"To support this, the state government has also allocated RM19.38 million for 25 drainage system projects, RM17.9 million for 16 river basin development and management projects, and RM6.63 million for nine environmentally friendly drainage projects," he said.
He added that road and bridge construction must also be coordinated with DID.
"In Petaling, for example, the construction of bridges along Jalan Kubu Gajah and Gajah 16 is linked to the Sungai Subang flood mitigation project," he said.
He said the state government had proposed RM25 million for flood mitigation works under the Selangor Maritime Gateway (SMG) Zero Pollution Emission (ZPE) initiative to continue improving river capacity and water flow.
For the longer term, he said RS-2 had identified 354 flood-prone areas under the state's flood mitigation infrastructure agenda.
"Through the Selangor Flood Mitigation Plan (SelF MiP), we will prioritise areas based on risk across river basins, assess the effectiveness of completed projects and coordinate state-level works with the Federal Government," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang Education Dept probing teacher for alleged abuse of SPM candidate
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Education Department is investigating allegations that a teacher repeatedly slapped, pinched and insulted a Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia candidate.
Its director, Mohamad Dziauddin Mat Saad, said the Education Office at the district the incident had allegedly taken place has been instructed to carry out an investigation and prepare recommendations for further action and resolution.
"The district Education Office met with the student and family this afternoon. The Education Department will also extend its cooperation to the relevant authorities," he said in a statement.
The probe follows a viral social media post by a parent appealing to Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek.
In the post, the parent claimed the child, a student at SMK Penanti in Kubang Semang, was repeatedly slapped, pinched until bruised and humiliated by a teacher simply for failing to score well in the Principles of Accounting subject.
The parent added that the incident caused the student to lose self-confidence, become afraid to attend school and express a reluctance to sit for the SPM examination scheduled to begin next week.
Dziauddin said the department's immediate focus is on providing socioemotional guidance services to the student to help prepare for the upcoming examination.
He also urged all parties to support a safe ecosystem for both students and teachers, particularly as candidates enter the final phase of preparations for SPM 2026.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Foreign Minister Mohamad arrives in Manila for Asean summit preparations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan has arrived in Manila, the Philippines, to lead Malaysia's delegation to ministerial preparatory meetings ahead of the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits, scheduled for Nov 15 to 17.
Wisma Putra said in a Facebook post that the meetings were an important part of Asean's diplomatic preparations, allowing ministers to review regional developments, discuss political and security issues and build consensus on matters to be considered by Asean leaders.
"For Malaysia, these negotiations are important to ensure Asean remains able to address regional challenges collectively. Through discussions with other Asean member states, Malaysia contributes to efforts to build consensus, address differences and lay the groundwork for discussions at leaders' level.
"The situation in Myanmar remains a priority requiring Asean's urgent attention, particularly efforts to achieve a peaceful solution through the implementation of Asean's Five-Point Consensus," it said.
Wisma Putra said the meetings would also provide a basis for discussions on regional stability, Asean cooperation and the challenges facing Southeast Asia.
Building on initiatives undertaken during Malaysia's Asean chairmanship in 2025, Malaysia would contribute to discussions on regional stability, Asean cooperation and the challenges facing the region, it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Alam Maritim forms pact to manage offshore transport in Asean, India
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Alam Maritim Resources Bhd's unit Subsea Worldwide Solutions Sdn Bhd has partnered with Singapore's Trident Oceanus Pte Ltd to manage offshore transportation and installation projects in Southeast Asia and the Indian subcontinent.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said both parties entered into a joint venture (JV) with Subsea holding a 70 per cent stake and Trident, the remaining 30 per cent stake.
The JV will have an initial issued and paid-up share capital of RM10,000 comprising 10,000 ordinary shares.
Trident was incorporated in January this year and specialises in offshore engineering and project management for the oil and gas and offshore renewable energy sectors.
The JV's board will comprise two directors with Subsea nominating two and one by Trident.
Subsea will also nominate the chairman of the board.
Alam Maritim's shares closed 2.22 per cent or half a sen lower at 22 sen, valuing the company at RM98.03 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man arrested after trespassing, vandalism at Petaling Jaya house
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A man was arrested after trespassing into a house and smashing a window in Jalan 5/17A, Petaling Jaya, this morning.
Petaling Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said the man, believed to be in his 30s, was found lying in the house compound.
He said police received information regarding the discovery of bloodstains in the compound at 9.25am.
"Investigations at the scene and witness statements revealed that the man is suspected of trespassing and breaking the house's window glass.
"The suspect was then arrested and taken to hospital for treatment as he was believed to have suffered injuries from the incident," he said in a statement today.
Shamsudin said the case is being investigated under Sections 447 and 427 of the Penal Code for criminal trespass and mischief causing damage.
Those with information can contact the nearest police station or the Petaling Jaya police headquarters operations room at 03-79662222 to assist investigations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Oil palm worker arrested after impregnating Year Six pupil
Article:
KABONG: Police have arrested a 28-year-old man after a 12-year-old Year Six pupil was found pregnant.
The case first came to light when the girl's mother brought her to school to inform the management of the pregnancy and said she wanted her daughter to leave school and marry the man.
Saratok police chief Deputy Superintendent Mathew Manggie said the headmistress referred the issue to the district Education Office, which instructed her to lodge a police report as the girl was still a minor.
He said preliminary investigations found that the man, who works as a labourer at an oil palm plantation, had known the girl since mid-2025 and was believed to have started a romantic relationship early this year.
"The victim admitted to having sexual intercourse with the suspect three times in mid-June," he said in a statement.
The girl reportedly discovered she was pregnant about a week ago and informed her mother on Nov 11.
Following the police report, a team from the Saratok Criminal Investigation Department, led by Inspector Henry Muji, tracked down the suspect and arrested him at a longhouse here.
The case is being investigated under Section 376 of the Penal Code for rape, which carries a jail term of up to 20 years, and whipping, upon conviction.

Title: Melaka polls: Ngwe makes final push to win over Machap Jaya voters [WATCH]
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Having been on the move since 9am, Barisan Nasional incumbent for Machap Jaya Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem is showing no signs of slowing down as campaigning enters its final hours ahead of tomorrow's polls.
With less than three hours before the campaign period ends, Ngwe is making a final push to reach as many constituents as possible.
He said his packed schedule was crucial to ensuring voters, including those who had returned from working elsewhere, were informed of his service record over the past five years.
"My schedule today is packed because I want to engage with as many voters as possible in Machap Jaya during these final hours before tonight's campaign deadline.
"Tonight is very important for me to explain to voters, especially young people returning from places such as Singapore and Kuala Lumpur, what I have accomplished as their elected representative over the past five years," he said.
Asked why constituents should retain him as their assemblyman, Ngwe cited his efforts to resolve a 30-year-old land dispute involving the former railway reserve in Melaka Pindah, which spans the Machap, Durian Tunggal, Rembia and Gadek state constituencies.
He also highlighted his efforts to safeguard the welfare and religious sensitivities of the Indian community by resolving two temple land issues in his constituency.
These included acquiring land within a private estate for a temple site to be gazetted. Indian voters make up 13.7 per cent of the electorate in Machap Jaya.
"As the assemblyman, I sought solutions through formal applications and land acquisition to secure proper temple land," he said.
"In Melaka, we do not take the approach seen in Selangor, where hundreds of temples were declared illegal," he added.
Ngwe said upgrading basic infrastructure in rural parts of Machap Jaya had remained a priority throughout his term. He cited the construction of new community halls and the installation of more than 100 solar-powered streetlights to improve visibility and safety at night.
He is defending the Machap Jaya seat in a three-cornered contest against Pakatan Harapan's Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin and Bersama's Prasanth Kumar Brakasam.
The semi-rural constituency has 16,030 registered voters across eight polling districts. Its electorate comprises 47 per cent Malays, 36 per cent Chinese, 13.7 per cent Indians and 3.3 per cent people from other ethnic groups.
Machap Jaya is one of only two seats in Melaka where male voters slightly outnumber female voters, accounting for 50.9 per cent and 49.1 per cent of the electorate respectively.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ab Rauf: BN-PN victory in Melaka will not affect federal government
Article:
MASJID TANAH: The federal government will remain unchanged if Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional win the Melaka election.
Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said the speculation arose after some quarters predicted that a new government could be formed following the strong cooperation between the two coalitions in the state election.
"If Melaka can contribute to a good election result through cooperation between Umno and Pas, some quarters would naturally expect a new government to be formed after the next general election.
"However, as things stand today, I do not see any indication that we will threaten the existing government," he said after taking part in a BN motorcycle convoy held as part of its flash mob programme here today.
In the Melaka election, BN and PN have forged a strategic electoral alliance, with BN contesting 23 of the 28 seats and PN fielding candidates in the remaining five.
In the 2021 state election, BN won 21 seats, securing a two-thirds majority, while Pakatan Harapan won five seats and PN took two.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Motul leverages MotoGP link at Sepang
Article:
MOTUL recently used the Malaysian Grand Prix 2026 at Sepang International Circuit to reinforce its long-standing association with MotoGP while showcasing its range of motorcycle lubricants and related products to local riders.
The race weekend, held from Oct 30 to Nov 1, attracted more than 196,000 spectators, providing motorcycle brands and industry players with a major platform to engage consumers.
Motul's display focused on products for different riding conditions, ranging from racing and long-distance touring to daily urban commuting.
Among the products featured were the Motul 300V 0W-30, Motul 7100 and Scooter Power LE MB lubricants.
The company said technologies developed and tested through motorsport are applied to products intended for everyday motorcycle use.
Motul Malaysia general manager Ravi Shankar said its involvement in MotoGP was a long-term commitment.
"Our involvement in MotoGP is a long-term commitment, and every season pushes us to raise the bar for what our products can do," he said.
"Seeing so many Malaysian riders at Sepang, from seasoned enthusiasts to everyday commuters, reminds us who that innovation is ultimately for."
The company also introduced its Motul GP Travel Kits, available in Chain and Helmet editions, during the race weekend.
Beyond its product displays, Motul organised a fan session on Oct 31 with Prima Pramac Racing Team riders Jack Miller and Augusto Fernández, attended by 80 fans.
The company also presented prizes under its "11 Weeks, 11 Bikes" campaign, with two participants receiving a Honda CB250R and a Peugeot Django Classic.
The campaign ran until Nov 8, offering a Kawasaki Ninja ZX-25RR as the grand prize.
Separately, the Peugeot Speedfight 4+ 150cc GP Edition was unveiled during the weekend.
The MotoGP-themed scooter will be limited to 50 units in Malaysia.
Motul is the official lubricant partner of Peugeot Motocycles in Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 37-year wait ends: Woman abandoned as baby confirmed as Malaysian citizen
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal has upheld a High Court decision declaring that a housewife, who was abandoned shortly after her birth before being adopted, is a Malaysian citizen.
A three-judge panel led by Datuk Seri Mohd Firuz Jaffril said the 37-year-old woman had crossed the threshold in proving she was indeed an abandoned baby.
He said there was no evidence before the court that the woman's biological mother was not permanently resident in the federation or at the place where she was found.
"We find no basis to disturb the High Court judge's finding that the respondent (the woman) was an abandoned infant within the meaning of Section 19B of Part III of the Second Schedule of the Federal Constitution.
Section 19B of Part II states that a newborn child found abandoned or exposed at a particular place is presumed to have been born at that place of a mother permanently residing at that place.
Firuz said the woman had fulfilled the requirements under Article 14 (1) (b) read together with Section 1 (a) of Part II and section 19B of Part III of the second schedule of the Federal Constitution.
"We are therefore satisfied that the respondent is a Malaysian citizen by operation of law," said Firuz, who sat with Datuk Ismail Brahim and Datuk Dean Wayne Daly.
In dismissing the appeals by the National Registration Department director-general, the home minister, Home Ministry and the government, he said the High Court had correctly appreciated the evidence and applied the principles laid down by the Federal Court in the case of CCH & Anor v Registrar of Births and Deaths.
That case, he said, establishes the approach in interpreting Section 19B.
The court ordered the appellants to pay RM10,000 in costs.
The woman was found abandoned shortly after birth in May 1989 in Kepong, Kuala Lumpur, and was raised by adoptive parents.
Following the registration of her adoption in 2009, NRD issued a birth certificate naming her adopted father as her father, but her citizenship status was recorded as "yet to be determined".
The Court of Appeal clarified that it is settled law that a person cannot obtain the right to citizenship by virtue of lawful adoptive parents, but the woman's entitlement arose from the constitutional presumption applicable to abandoned newborns.
Senior federal counsel Norazlinawati Mohd Arshad and federal counsel Jicent Yee Xin Sheng appeared for the government while lawyers M. Yogamani and M. Shahgambahri represented the woman.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Six family members among seven charged over parking dispute brawl
Article:
BATU PAHAT: Six family members were among seven people charged at the magistrate's court here today with jointly participating in a brawl over a parking dispute in September.
Siti Jumaidah Samsudin, 41; Mohamad Nor Hashim, 38; Norlaileasma Md Baharom, 44; Bitah A Kadir, 75; Aina Maisara Anuar, 19; Aina Aliesya, 20; and a 17-year-old boy pleaded not guilty after the charge was read out before magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno.
They were accused of fighting in a public place at Kampung Parit Bilal at 8.40pm on Sept 27.
The charge was framed under Section 160 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same code, which carries a maximum jail term of six months, a fine of up to RM1,000, or both, upon conviction.
According to the facts of the case, Siti Jumaidah, who was also the complainant, was visiting her younger sibling's house when a dispute broke out over customers of a nearby eatery parking their vehicles in front of the house.
Several acquaintances later arrived at the house and expressed dissatisfaction with Siti Jumaidah's sibling over the parking issue.
During the altercation, Siti Jumaidah was allegedly hit and pulled, leaving her with facial injuries and a sprained left arm.
She later sought treatment at Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital here.
The incident was also captured by a closed-circuit television (CCTV) camera installed at a nearby house.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Shahzleen Ibrahim prosecuted, while all seven accused were unrepresented.
The court granted Siti Jumaidah bail of RM1,000, while the other six accused were each granted bail of RM500.
The case was fixed for mention on Jan 15 for document submission and the appointment of counsel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 5,632 contract teachers receive permanent appointment offers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More than 5,600 of the 5,840 Education Service Officers appointed on a contract-of-service (CoS) basis in 2023 have received offers of permanent appointments as of Nov 12.
The Education Ministry said the Education Services Commission had approved contract extensions for all 5,840 officers still in service, effective the day after their original contracts expired.
"This allows all the officers concerned to continue serving and receive their emoluments as usual," it said in a statement today.
The ministry said, of the total number, 5,632 have since been offered permanent appointments.
It added that 29 officers were still undergoing processing by the commission while another 179 had yet to fulfil the requirements for permanent appointments.
These included officers who had yet to obtain professional qualifications or the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR) C1 qualification for those specialising in English.
The ministry said no permanent posting instructions had been issued so far, with all postings scheduled to be issued only next month.
"As such, no officers will be given priority based on any state or district," it said.
Officers were told to continue reporting for duty as usual while awaiting their posting instructions.
Earlier, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek had said
1,799 out of 1,832 teachers
who have yet to meet the requirements for confirmation in service failed a mandatory assessment.
She had said teachers must fulfil several conditions before being confirmed as permanent members of the civil service.
She said the Education Ministry was working closely with the commission to ensure the appointment, confirmation and placement of teachers were handled systematically and in accordance with existing regulations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former MAG chief Izham Ismail appointed to Maybank board
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has appointed former Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) group managing director and airline group chief executive officer Datuk Captain Izham Ismail as an independent non-executive director effective Nov 15.
Maybank announced the appointment in a Bursa Malaysia filing today.
Izham, 65, led MAG as group managing director and airline group CEO from 2017 until 2026, retiring from the airline group on Jan 31 this year.
A veteran of Malaysia's aviation industry, he joined Malaysia Airlines as a pilot in 1979 before moving into a series of senior operational and management roles.
Among his previous positions were chief revenue officer from 2019 to 2023, group chief operations officer between 2016 and 2017, and chief executive officer of MASwings Sdn Bhd in 2016.
His appointment brings extensive aviation, operational and corporate leadership experience to the board of Malaysia's largest banking group.
According to the filing, Izham does not hold any other directorships in public companies or listed issuers and has no interest in Maybank securities.
The appointment comes as Maybank navigates a softer earnings performance in the first half of its 2026 financial year.
For the six months ended June 30, 2026, Maybank's net profit edged down to RM5.17 billion from RM5.22 billion in the corresponding period a year earlier.
Revenue fell 8.7 per cent to RM30.99 billion, compared with RM33.95 billion previously
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor allocates RM559mil to replace ageing water pipes
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Selangor has allocated RM559 million in its 2027 Budget to replace ageing water pipes as part of efforts to improve the state's water supply system.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said more than 6,000km of ageing pipes needed to be replaced, with 1,231.01km already replaced as of August 2026.
The annual replacement target was increased from 150km to 300km in 2024 to speed up the programme, which began in 2016.
Another RM143.2 million has been allocated to upgrade water treatment plants, while RM209.2 million will go towards the Water Grid Connectivity project.
The project aims to achieve 100 per cent connectivity for 36 dam terminals by the end of 2028, strengthening the water supply systems in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.
Separately, the state government will provide a RM250 million loan to Worldwide Holdings Berhad to build its third Waste-to-Energy plant in Tanjung Dua Belas, which will include a recycling materials recovery facility.
The second Waste-to-Energy plant is scheduled to begin operations in the first quarter of 2027. It will have the capacity to process 3,000 tonnes of waste a day and generate 52 megawatts of electricity.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor to give 5,000 p-hailing riders RM100 monthly voucher
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Some 5,000 registered p-hailing riders in Selangor will receive RM100 monthly, or RM1,200 annually, under the Kita Selangor Gig Voucher initiative announced in the Selangor 2027 Budget.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the initiative recognised the riders' contribution to the logistics sector and the income risks they faced due to illness or accidents.
He said many gig workers continued to struggle to secure permanent employment, partly because their skills did not match industry requirements.
"To address this challenge, the state government will provide the Kita Selangor Gig Voucher of RM100 a month, equivalent to RM1,200 a year, to 5,000 registered p-hailing riders to ease their financial burden," he said when tabling the RM3.3 billion Selangor 2027 Budget at the state legislative assembly sitting here today.
Amirudin said the voucher would be complemented by technology exposure and industry training through short courses conducted by the Selangor Technical Skills Development Centre (STDC).
The programme, including training, would receive an allocation of RM10 million, he said.
Meanwhile, the state government has allocated RM12 million to help residents harness productivity gains from artificial intelligence (AI).
In collaboration with STDC and Google, the state will provide 50,000 Selangorians with one-year access to Gemini Enterprise, alongside online and in-person training.
Amirudin said the programme would equip participants from various backgrounds, including students, entrepreneurs, farmers, start-up founders and senior citizens, with skills to develop agentic AI systems to improve productivity and simplify daily tasks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Seventh victim found after water surge at Sungai Pertak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The body of an Indian citizen was found during a search and rescue operation following a water surge at Sungai Luit, Kampung Orang Asli Pertak, Kuala Kubu Baru.
The discovery brings the number of victims found to seven out of eight, with one man still missing.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department director Datuk Wan Md Razali Wan Ismail said the seventh body was found at 3.40pm in Sector C of the search area.
He said the body was taken to Sungai Buloh Hospital.
The search and rescue operation is continuing to find the remaining missing victim.
Eight men, including one Malaysian and seven foreigners, were swept away by strong currents during a water surge at Sungai Luit last Monday.
Five victims were found on Tuesday, while the
sixth body was recovered near the Sungai Selangor Dam
yesterday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PKR leaders slam Hadi over remarks comparing Muslim, non-Muslim leaders, question PAS ties with MCA, Gerakan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Several PKR leaders have criticised PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang over his remarks comparing Muslim and non-Muslim leaders, warning that religious sentiments should not be used to divide Malaysians for political gain.
PKR vice-president Datuk Chang Lih Kang said political differences should be debated based on policies and solutions to people’s problems rather than religious sentiments.
He described Abdul Hadi’s remarks during a Melaka state election campaign event yesterday as deeply disappointing, saying statements that hurt religious sensitivities and fuel tensions would only harm the country.
Abdul Hadi was quoted as saying that even the worst Muslim leaders governing a country would not be as oppressive as non-Muslims.
“As a religious figure with extensive knowledge, he should set an example in promoting good character and unity. Unfortunately, that knowledge is not reflected in the wisdom of his words,” Chang said in a statement today.
Chang, who is also Science, Technology and Innovation Minister, said Malaysia’s multiracial and multireligious harmony was essential to economic development, investor confidence and job creation.
He questioned whether the pursuit of political power should come at the expense of national unity and stability, stressing that Malaysia needed leaders who brought people together rather than divided them.
Meanwhile, PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh questioned how Abdul Hadi’s remarks aligned with opposition political cooperation in Melaka, particularly involving MCA and Gerakan in the campaign for Kelebang seat.
“Interestingly, the MCA president had spoken at the same campaign event, while Gerakan president Dominic Lau also appealed to Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional supporters to back a non-Muslim Gerakan candidate.
“This happened in front of a Malay-majority audience. So, how should Abdul Hadi’s remarks be interpreted in the context of their political cooperation?” said Fuziah, who is also Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister.
Fuziah also expressed support for Pakatan Harapan’s candidate for Kelebang, Farzana Hayani, saying that her links to the federal ruling coalition could help bring local concerns to the government’s attention regardless of race or religion.
Separately, PKR Youth (AMK) chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim described Abdul Hadi’s remarks as extreme and prejudiced, warning that they could fuel religious hostility and undermine national unity.
He noted that it is all the more concerning that such a statement came from a senior political leader who possesses a background in religious education and wields significant influence within the Muslim community.
“Such a position and level of knowledge should be used to foster an understanding of Islam rooted in justice, wisdom, and noble character, not to cultivate the perception that a Muslim possesses an absolute moral superiority over followers of other religions, even when committing acts of injustice,” he said in a statement.
He said that the AMK views the attempt to weigh the severity of an injustice based on religious identity as a departure from the principle of justice, a fundamental tenet of Islamic teachings. Furthermore, it raises questions regarding the party’s sincerity in building political cooperation across racial and religious lines.
“Do such views also apply to the leaders of the MCA and Gerakan, who are PAS’s political partners? Or is this principle applied only when dealing with those who hold opposing political stances?” he asked.
As such, Muhammad Kamil urged Abdul Hadi to publicly clarify and retract his remarks, saying justice should apply equally regardless of race, religion or political affiliation.
He stressed that Malaysia’s future must be grounded in constitutional principles, respect for Islam as the religion of the Federation and the protection of religious freedom for all citizens.
“Justice does not discriminate based on the perpetrator’s skin colour, lineage, or religion; indeed, injustice must be opposed, even when committed by those of the same race, religion, or political persuasion,” he added.
Meanwhile, Sabah Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Mustapha Sakmud described Abdul Hadi’s statement as extreme, out of bounds and completely unacceptable.
“Such remarks not only offend followers of other religions, but could also disrupt the harmony of Malaysia’s multiracial society, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak, which have long lived in an atmosphere of mutual respect regardless of religion, race and culture.
“In Sabah, there is no place for politics that discriminates against followers of other religions, as religious differences are not a barrier to family ties, friendship and community life,” he said.
He said a family in Sabah can have members who practise different faiths, yet they still live in harmony and mutual respect.
Mustapha stressed that Islam teaches its followers to be just to all people regardless of religion, adding that a leader’s justice or tyranny must be judged by their actions and integrity, not the faith they profess.
“As a political leader and religious figure, Abdul Hadi should act responsibly and refrain from making statements that could arouse prejudice and undermine social harmony,” he said.
Mustapha urged Sabahans and all Malaysians, particularly the people of Melaka, to remain vigilant and reject political parties that preach hatred against followers of other religions. — Bernama

Title: HKL monitors cop after successful hand reattachment following Kepong machete attack
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The Ministry of Health (MOH), through the Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL), is closely monitoring the recovery of a policeman whose hand was reattached following an attack on Wednesday (November 11).
HKL director Datuk Dr Harikrishna K. Ragavan Nair said the policeman was referred to the hospital for specialist treatment and immediately taken to the Main Operating Theatre for surgery after thorough examination and assessment by a team of specialists.
He said the eight-hour surgery involved reattaching injured blood vessels and nerve structures, as well as restoring the anatomical structure of the affected hand.
“The surgery was led by HKL Upper Limb and Microsurgery subspecialists Dr R. Allan Ravi and Dr Aziz Sabbir Husain, in collaboration with the entire HKL Upper Limb and Microsurgery Unit team and the anaesthesiology team,” he said in a statement here today.
Harikrishna said the case involved a complex procedure requiring specialised expertise, advanced microsurgical skills and close multidisciplinary collaboration to ensure comprehensive and optimal treatment.
He added that HKL remains committed to providing high-quality treatment services through multidisciplinary expertise, technology and professional skills for the wellbeing of the community.
On Wednesday, the policeman’s right hand was severed at the wrist after he was attacked by a foreign man armed with a machete at a residential premises in Desa Aman Puri, Kepong. — Bernama

Title: Body of Indian national found, seventh victim of Sungai Pertak water surge, one still missing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The body of the seventh victim of the water surge incident at the Sungai Pertak Picnic Site near here was found at 3.40pm today, leaving only one of the eight people reported missing still unaccounted for.
According to the latest information from the Incident Command Post (PKTK), the body of the adult Indian national was found in Sector C of the search area.
The victim was pronounced dead by an assistant medical officer from the Rasa Health Clinic at 4.45pm after being brought to the PKTK.
The body was subsequently handed over to the police at 4.59pm before being taken to Sungai Buloh Hospital for a post-mortem.
Following the discovery, the search and rescue (SAR) operation, now in its fifth day, continued with the focus on Sectors C and D to locate the remaining missing victim.
Today’s SAR operation began at 7am, with additional personnel from the Special Tactical Operations and Rescue Team Malaysia of the Fire and Rescue Department.
Also deployed were the Selangor Special Incident and Emergency Response Rapid Team of the Malaysian Civil Defence Force and Forestry Department Mountain Guides, as well as two drone units from the Air Operations Force to assist in searching the water surface.
Yesterday, the body of the sixth victim, identified as a Yemeni national, was found floating at 10.15am at the river mouth near the Pertak Bridge.
In the incident at about 5.30pm last Monday, eight men, comprising one local and seven foreigners from Yemen, Sri Lanka, Nepal and India, were reported missing after being swept away by strong currents. — Bernama

Title: Report: Najib spent nearly eight hours out of Taman Duta residence for Friday prayers, returns at 6.27pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, who is under house arrest, returned to his residence in Taman Duta at about 6.27pm today, concluding an outing that lasted nearly eight hours.
Najib left his home at approximately 10.28am and was escorted directly by prison department vehicles, Chinese-language newspaper
Sin Chew Daily
reported this evening.
He was spotted leaving for Friday prayers this morning before making his way back to his residence in the evening.
Najib, convicted of abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving RM42 million of SRC International Sdn Bhd funds, is serving the remainder of his six-year sentence under house arrest at his Jalan Langgak Duta residence until August 23, 2028, following a conditional royal pardon granted in September.
Under the strict conditions set by the Pardons Board, he is barred from engaging in political activities, making media statements, or appearing on social media.
He is also prohibited from leaving the gazetted premises without written permission, although prison officers are permitted to escort him for Friday prayers.

Title: Amirudin unveils ‘Kita Selangor’ special financial aid with two months’ salary for civil servants, minimum RM1,000
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 13 — The Selangor State Government today announced a Special Financial Assistance (BKK) equivalent to two months’ salary for civil servants in the state.
Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said this incentive serves as a token of appreciation for the hard work of civil servants in delivering aid to the people, particularly through the implementation of the Pakej Pengukuhan Daya Tahan Selangor.
He noted that the implementation of this package has helped empower vulnerable groups, school students, working women, farmers, and padi farmers as they navigate the global energy crisis.
“The state government is announcing the ‘Kita Selangor’ Special Financial Assistance (BKK) for the year 2026, amounting to two months’ salary or allowance, with a minimum payment of RM1,000.
“This payment will be drawn from current-year allocations and will cover the emoluments of state government personnel including those whose salaries are paid by the federal government as well as teachers of ‘Kelas Al-Quran dan Fardu Ain’ (KAFA) religious classes, with a total financial implication of RM100.31 million.
“God willing, the ‘Kita Selangor’ BKK will be disbursed by December 21,” he said while tabling the Selangor Budget 2027 today.
Meanwhile, Amirudin said the state government proposed an increase in the monthly allowance for KAFA teachers by RM200, raising the total allowance from RM1,500 to RM1,700 starting from January 2027.
He said the proposal would involve 7,245 KAFA teachers appointed by the state and the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM), including 4,303 JAIS Fardhu Ain Teachers (GAF) and 2,942 JAKIM KAFA Teachers.
“The Selangor State Government always recognises the contributions and sacrifices of KAFA teachers as the main pillar in shaping a generation that is knowledgeable, faithful and of noble character. Therefore, the welfare and well-being of religious educators must continue to be prioritised, especially in facing the rising cost of living.
“This initiative is an initial step towards aligning the welfare of religious educators while appreciating their role in educating more than 100,000 students throughout Selangor. The increase in this allowance involves an additional financial implication of RM14 million, which will be covered by the state government,” he said.
He also said that the state government also plans to increase the allowance for KAFA teacher — those appointed by the state as well as by JAKIM — to RM2,000, in line with the new federal minimum wage rate that will take effect from June 2027. — Bernama

Title: Amirudin: Sungai Klang, Sungai Langat among river basins in Selangor’s RM36.45m flood mitigation plan
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 13 — The Selangor government has allocated RM36.45 million for 47 immediate flood mitigation projects under the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS) for 2027.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, when tabling the state’s Budget 2027, said that of the total, RM9.15 million would be for the Sungai Klang basin and RM7.35 million for the development of the Sungai Langat basin.
He said the allocation would also cover the Sungai Buloh, Sungai Selangor, Sungai Bernam and Sungai Kapar Besar river basins, as well as preparatory works such as design, surveying and land matters.
He added that, of the 47 projects, 30 are continuation projects, of which 13 have been completed and are undergoing final account preparation, nine are being implemented, two are at the pre-tender stage while six are at the design stage.
“As for the 17 new projects, one is at the design stage, 11 are in the process of appointing consultants and five are still at the planning stage,” he said at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly sitting today.
Amirudin also said that RM19.38 million had been allocated for 25 irrigation system projects, RM17.90 million for 16 river basin development and management projects, and RM6.63 million for nine environmentally friendly irrigation projects.
For flood mitigation projects under the Selangor Maritime Gateway Economic Development Zone (SMG ZPE), RM25 million has been proposed to continue works to increase river capacity and improve water flow, with the projects having achieved 71.43 per cent physical progress.
While physical works are underway, Amirudin said the disaster warning system between the state and district operation centres and agencies on the ground would also be improved.
“Through the Community-Based Disaster Risk Management Programme and training in schools, we want residents to know where they need to go, who to contact and how to assist those who need support to evacuate,” he added.
Amirudin also wants the Public Works Department (JKR), local authorities (PBTs) and the JPS to prioritise projects that resolves flooding problems, including culverts and drainage systems.
“Technical reviews that can be conducted concurrently should be initiated simultaneously. If a decision involves multiple agencies, the matter must be brought to the relevant authorities who can resolve it at an earlier stage.
“The Netherlands’ experience offers us a guide on what needs to be accelerated and one of the initiatives is the integration of embankments and water control structures with planning that allows rivers to overflow more safely,” he added.
Meanwhile, he said the state government would provide a public dashboard displaying project locations, implementing agencies and updates on implementation phases, from the appointment of design consultants and contractors to the progress of on-site works.
“Before the monsoon season begins, the government will update the status of flood-prone locations, detailing the related projects, appointments that have been made and works expected to be completed in time.
“With this information, residents can know the level of protection in their areas ahead of the rainy season and refer directly to the agencies responsible,” he said. — Bernama

Title: MB: Selangor budgets RM559m for 6,000km of ageing pipes, RM3.5m for water master plan
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 13 — The Selangor government has allocated RM559 million next year to replace ageing pipes in the state to ensure a more stable water supply for consumers.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said more than 6,000 kilometres (km) of ageing pipes needed replacing, and the state government has increased its annual allocation starting from 2024 to expedite the effort.
“The pipe replacement programme was first implemented in 2016, with an annual target of replacing 150km of pipes.
“However, starting from 2024, the state government and Air Selangor Sdn Bhd (Air Selangor) have increased the replacement rate to 300km annually,” he said when tabling the Selangor 2027 Budget here today.
He said a total of 1,231.01km of ageing pipes had been replaced as of August this year.
Meanwhile, Amirudin said the state government had also allocated RM120.8 million for the Non-Revenue Water (NRW) Reduction Programme, which includes the installation of Pressure Transient and Permanent Leak Noise Correlating Loggers (PLNCL) and Advanced Pressure Management Systems (APMS).
“The NRW rate is targeted to be reduced to 26.3 per cent this year and 25.8 per cent in 2027, compared with 26.8 per cent in 2025.
“The annual reduction of 0.5 percentage points is in line with the target set by Air Selangor and submitted to the National Water Services Commission (SPAN),” he said.
Amirudin said the state government had also allocated RM101 million to further ensure a clean water supply, including through the Raw Water Guarantee Scheme, which aims to protect water treatment plant operations from disruptions caused by pollution.
In addition, he said RM3.5 million had been allocated for a study on the Selangor Water Master Plan 2025-2050 as part of long-term planning. The master plan will coordinate the management of raw water, treated water and wastewater with flood management and is expected to be completed in 2028. — Bernama

Title: Selangor allocates RM24m to boost public transport use to 60pc, says MB
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 13 — The Selangor state government has allocated RM24 million for the public transport sector in 2027, aiming to increase public transport usage among state residents to 60 per cent from the current 40 per cent.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the allocation would support efforts to develop a more people-friendly public transport ecosystem, including improving bus services, providing fare subsidies and expanding pedestrian routes.
He said that although public transport officially came under the jurisdiction of the federal government, Selangor, with a population of nearly 7.5 million, needed to take proactive steps to complement federal-level efforts.
“To develop a well-structured first- and last-mile connectivity system that complements a comprehensive public transport ecosystem in Selangor, the state government has allocated RM24 million for the sector in 2027,” he said when tabling the Selangor Budget 2027 at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly here today.
Amirudin said RM12 million had been allocated to improve the efficiency and optimise the routes of the Smart Selangor Bus service, which would be rebranded as Bas Kita Selangor.
He said the improvements would include more systematic route management and increased service frequency to connect residents to rail stations and key areas in the state.
He said the state government would also introduce the SEL 30 Programme in 2027, with an allocation of RM5 million to provide a RM30 monthly public transport subsidy, expected to benefit 13,000 users.
The programme aims to reduce travel costs for Selangor residents while encouraging more people to use bus and rail services.
To improve access to public transport, Amirudin said the state government, through local authorities, would build 35 kilometres of new pedestrian walkways across Selangor to facilitate access to key destinations, including public transport stations.
He said the Pedestrian Audit would also be completed by the end of this year and used as a reference to address issues concerning pedestrian facilities and walkway safety.
In addition, the state government would introduce Selangor Mobility Nexus, an integrated mobility data and information centre to make public transport information more accessible through a single system.
Amirudin said the initiative aimed to reduce duplication among existing applications and systems, enabling users to check bus stop locations, arrival times and route information more easily.
He said the development of Selangor Mobility Nexus would be supported by Rantaian Mesra Sdn Bhd at a cost of RM1.5 million, focusing on data integration, including journey planning, Scan-to-Ride, complaint management and mobility route mapping. — Bernama

Title: Federal Court sets Feb 25 to hear Altantuya family’s leave to appeal over reduced RM1.4m award
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 13 — The Federal Court has fixed February 25 next year to hear an application by the family of murdered Mongolian national Altantuya Shaariibuu for leave to appeal against a Court of Appeal ruling that reduced the damages awarded over her death in 2006.
Lawyer Abraham Au, representing political analyst Abdul Razak Baginda, confirmed the date when contacted by Bernama.
He said the court also set Dec 3 to hear the family’s application to amend its notice of motion seeking leave to appeal, following case management before Federal Court deputy registrar Rohaiza Hamzah yesterday.
Altantuya’s family filed the leave application on February 19 this year after the Court of Appeal reduced the damages awarded to them from RM5 million to RM1.4 million.
On January 20, the appellate court also ruled that the government was not vicariously liable for the actions of former police officers Sirul Azhar Umar and Azilah Hadri.
The family filed a RM100 million civil suit against Abdul Razak, Azilah, Sirul Azhar and the government in 2007, claiming that Altantuya’s death had caused them mental shock and psychological trauma.
In 2022, the Shah Alam High Court ordered the defendants to pay RM5 million in damages to the family.
Azilah and Sirul Azhar were convicted of Altantuya’s murder in 2009. The Court of Appeal subsequently acquitted them, but the Federal Court overturned the acquittals and reinstated their convictions in 2015.
In 2023, the Federal Court commuted Azilah’s death sentence to 40 years’ imprisonment after allowing his review application under the Revision of Sentence of Death and Imprisonment for Natural Life (Temporary Jurisdiction of the Federal Court) Act 2023. — Bernama

Title: It’s final: Dutch model Ivana Smit’s mother stops pursuing lawsuit against govt over probe of 2017 death
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The late Dutch model Ivana Smit’s family has decided to not continue pursuing a lawsuit against the Malaysian government at the Federal Court over alleged negligence in a probe of her 2017 death, the family’s lawyer Datuk Sankara Nair confirmed today.
This brings Smit’s family’s six-year legal bid in court to an end, but Sankara said the authorities should continue to investigate her death and to regularly communicate with her family.
“Ivana’s family has decided not to seek leave to appeal to the Federal Court against the Court of Appeal’s decision of October 14, 2026. Accordingly, these civil proceedings have come to an end.
“Their decision deserves respect and should not be understood as satisfaction with the investigation or acceptance that their concerns have been answered,” he said in a statement today.
Tomorrow would be the last day to file for leave to appeal the Court of Appeal’s October 14 decision, and not filing for it would mean the family is not pursuing the lawsuit.
The Court of Appeal decision was not in Smit’s family’s favour.
But Sankara today also commended the Court of Appeal for its “firm, emphatic and stern” verbal remarks when delivering its decision on October 14, where it cautioned that this does not exonerate past shortcomings and emphasised the police’s continuing responsibility to pursue viable leads diligently and keep the family regularly informed.
He made it clear that the court had made these observations orally, and that this was not part of a formal or written order that directed the police to give updates to Smit’s family.
“The conclusion of this civil action leaves the authorities’ investigative responsibilities intact. We call upon them to heed the Court’s oral observations through sustained investigative effort and clear, regular communication with Ivana’s family.
“The family has chosen to bring its civil litigation to a close. The authorities must continue their work towards establishing the truth surrounding Ivana’s death,” he concluded in the statement.
Tomorrow would be the last day to file for leave to appeal the Court of Appeal’s October 14 decision, and not filing for it would mean the family is not pursuing the lawsuit. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
What happened before this
On December 7, 2017, 18-year-old Smit was found nude and dead on the sixth floor of CapSquare Residence, a condominium off Jalan Dang Wangi in Kuala Lumpur, after having fallen from a unit on the 20th floor.
The Coroner’s Court on March 18, 2019 in an inquest found that Smit’s death was caused by a “misadventure”.
But the High Court on November 22, 2019 replaced the inquest findings by saying that Smit’s death was caused by “a person or persons unknown”, and ordered the police to start investigations again.
In November 2020, Smit’s mother Christina Carolina Gerarda Johanna Verstappen filed a civil suit against the inspector-general of police, Dang Wangi investigating officer ASP Faizal Abdullah, the home minister, and the Malaysian government over alleged breach of duties and negligence in investigating the cause of her daughter’s 2017 death.
On July 29, 2025, the High Court ordered all those sued to pay RM1.1 million compensation, and declared the police as having failed to carry out their duties to restart investigations as ordered in 2019.
Also on July 29, 2025, the High Court issued a court order known as a “mandamus order”, which included ordering the police to restart investigations on Smit’s death and to brief the Attorney General’s Chambers every three months with updates on the investigation.
On October 14, 2026, the Court of Appeal set aside the High Court’s decision, including the RM1.1 million award.
Among other things, the Court of Appeal reportedly ruled that the police’s public duty to investigate crime does not give rise to a private duty of care that would result in compensation to individual victims or their relatives for perceived investigation failures.
The Court of Appeal had also ruled that the decisions from the inquest and the 2019 criminal revision at the High Court could not by themselves establish civil liability in a separate case, Sankara said today.
In his statement today, Sankara also said the Court of Appeal’s October 14 decision does not mean that public authorities would have blanket immunity, but said it is a “substantial obstacle” for families who are pursuing such court claims over alleged negligence in investigations of deaths.
“We respectfully recognise the courts’ responsibility to apply established legal principles. Nevertheless, concerns about exposing public authorities to excessive litigation must be weighed against the need for meaningful accountability.
“A public duty must carry practical substance for the people it exists to protect. Where the law restricts civil redress, the case for effective independent oversight and legislative consideration becomes all the more pressing and compelling,” he said in the same statement.
