Title: Melaka polls: 240 polling centres to open tomorrow for 675,166 electors, says EC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — A total of 240 polling centres involving 1,213 streams across Melaka will open tomorrow for 675,166 registered electors to cast their ballots in the 16th Melaka State Election.
Election Commission (EC) secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said 11,103 personnel have been assigned to ensure smooth voting at all the polling centres.
He said the EC has also completed checking all voting equipment, including ballot boxes, election ink, ballot papers and voting booths, ensuring they are in good condition before distribution to Presiding Officers (KTM) at each stream.
“Voters are advised not to wait until the last minute and are encouraged to vote according to the Recommended Voting Time stated on the MySPR Semak application.
“However, voters may still cast their ballots at their convenience from 8 am to 6pm,” he said in a statement today.
Khairul Shahril also reminded voters to bring their identity cards and voting details to show to the First Polling Clerk (KP1) at their stream to facilitate verification, and not to hand over their identity cards to anyone other than election workers.
Voters are also advised to check their polling centre, stream and sequence number early through the portal https://mysprsemak.spr.gov.my, the MySPR Semak application or by calling the EC hotline at 03-8892 7218.
At the same time, the EC reminded employers to allow a reasonable period for registered employees to go out and vote tomorrow, as provided under the Election Offences Act 1954.
Meanwhile, he said the official campaign period ends at 11.59pm tonight, and all contesting parties must cease any form of campaigning, including soliciting votes outside polling centres or on social media platforms such as Facebook, X, Instagram, TikTok and Threads.
“The EC also reminds all contesting parties and candidates that they are prohibited from opening, setting up or maintaining booths on Polling Day, as doing so is an offence under the Election Offences Act 1954,” he said.
On polling centre procedures, Khairul Shahril said the use of mobile phones inside voting streams is prohibited, and voters must place their devices in the designated area after receiving their ballot papers before collecting them once they have voted.
In addition, voters, candidates and workers are barred from wearing shirts, caps or face masks, or bringing any materials displaying the name, logo, symbol or photograph of a party or candidate, as well as campaign slogans, into polling centres.
“Failure by voters to comply with or any breach of the stipulated regulations may result in election workers barring them from entering the polling centre,” he said.
Meanwhile, he said the EC will continue the comprehensive pilot implementation of the Optical Character Recognition — Voter Attendance (OCR-VA) system across all voting streams to speed up verification and digitally record attendance without altering existing voting procedures.
The public and stakeholders can also monitor real-time voter turnout throughout tomorrow at https://dashboard.spr.gov.my, while official results for all 28 state constituencies will be announced once the official vote-tallying process is completed.
Get the latest news on the 16th Melaka State Election at https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Morning cloudy weather; some afternoon thunderstorms, says MetMalaysia
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 13 — The 16th Melaka State Election will be held tomorrow, and the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecasts that all three districts in the state, namely Melaka Tengah, Jasin and Alor Gajah, will experience cloudy weather in the morning.
MetMalaysia, through its official portal, also forecasts that several places in these three districts will experience thunderstorms in the afternoon.
According to the Election Commission (EC), a total of 675,166 ordinary voters are eligible to fulfil their responsibilities on polling day tomorrow, with an expected voter turnout of 70 per cent.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026 — Bernama

Title: UEC holders: No change to entry requirements for private medical degrees, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The government has agreed today to maintain the existing minimum entry requirements for Unified Examination Certificate (UEC) holders seeking admission into medical programmes at private higher education institutions.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the decision was agreed to during a Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today.
He said the decision is consistent with the government’s previous requirements and retains the same criteria that existed prior to any amendments.
Fahmi, who is also the unity government spokesman, said UEC holders who meet the minimum requirement of a ‘B4’ grade in five specified subjects remain eligible to apply for admission into medical degree programmes at private higher education institutions.
“The Cabinet agreed to maintain the minimum entry requirements for UEC holders intending to pursue medical programmes,” he said during a post-Cabinet media conference that was broadcast live today.
A B4 is the minimum UEC grade required in each of five compulsory subjects: Biology, Chemistry, Physics, and Mathematics (or Advanced Mathematics I and II, or Advanced Mathematics).
Fahmi added that the Health Ministry and the Malaysian Medical Council (MMC) will coordinate any administrative issues with the Higher Education Ministry to ensure the smooth implementation based on the decision.
He explained that the effort is intended to address any emerging issues.
“It is also to ensure that the standards and quality of medical education in the country, including at private higher education institutions, are upheld,” he said.
The UEC qualification remains unrecognised by the government as an entry qualification for admission to any public universities.
However, UEC holders remain eligible for direct admission into medical degree programmes (such as MBBS or MD) at private higher education institutions in Malaysia, provided they also meet SPM/UEC credit requirements for Bahasa Malaysia and English as mandated by MMC.

Title: Cabinet seeks AG’s advice on proposal to declassify Najib’s pardon board minutes, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The process of declassifying documents from the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting concerning former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak is underway and being carried out in accordance with existing laws, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
Fahmi, who is also the unity government spokesman, said various legal requirements must be fulfilled before a final decision can be made.
“It (the matter) was not explicitly raised during today’s Cabinet meeting, but I understand that the process is underway.
“The Cabinet has sought advice from Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar and the process will adhere to the mandatory procedures,” he said during a post-Cabinet media conference that was broadcasted live today.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail was reported as saying in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday that he would put forward the proposal to declassify Najib’s Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting minutes to the Cabinet for consideration.
He said he had no objection to bringing the proposal before the Cabinet, although the matter fell under the purview of the Attorney General.
Saifuddin had earlier described a suggestion by Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman to disclose the minutes as a good recommendation, saying it could provide a clearer and more transparent picture of the process.
The proposal comes amid controversy surrounding Najib’s conditional pardon, which allows him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International case under under house arrest.

Title: Melaka polls: Stop all campaigning by 11.59pm tonight, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 13 — All candidates contesting the 16th Melaka State Election have been reminded to cease all campaign activities, including on social media platforms, by 11.59pm tonight, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said the Election Commission (EC) reminder must be complied with, meaning no new posts or content that could be construed as campaigning should appear on candidates’ social media accounts from midnight tonight through tomorrow.
“So, no new posts on social media nearing midnight tonight. Put your messages up early; no one should campaign or post anything that could be interpreted as campaigning, including on social media accounts, tomorrow,” he said during his weekly press conference here today.
Fahmi, who is also Madani Government spokesman, said the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will continue monitoring to ensure there are no legal violations, including on social media.
Meanwhile, Fahmi advised voters to turn out early in view of forecast rain on polling day.
“For those travelling back to their hometowns to vote in Melaka, drive safely, ensure you get enough rest, make sure your vehicles are well-maintained and do not exceed the speed limit,” he said.
He also urged the public to refer to the EC’s official social media accounts, including on Facebook, Threads and X, for updates on the Melaka state election, as well as to obtain information from verified mainstream media sources.
“Refer to the official webpages and obtain information from verified mainstream media sources, not dubious accounts appearing on social media, as it is not impossible that certain parties may produce content of questionable authenticity,” he said.
Some 675,166 ordinary electors are eligible to cast their ballots tomorrow, with voter turnout expected to reach 70 per cent. — Bernama

Title: Anwar concerned over safety protocols for police following Kepong attack, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed concern over the safety of police officers following an incident in Kepong two days ago in which a police officer was attacked and had his right hand severed.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said existing procedures allow police officers to take necessary action to protect themselves.
He added that Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail had also clarified that current protocols allow police officers to prioritise their own safety.
“The Cabinet was informed today that a seven-hour surgery to reattach the police officer’s hand at Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) was successful,” he said during a post-Cabinet media conference broadcast live today.
Fahmi, who is also the unity government spokesman, added that the Cabinet was informed that the officer was making a positive recovery.
He said the officer was also able to move several fingers on his affected hand following the reattachment operation.
“Nevertheless, the prime minister remains very concerned about the incident,” he said.
The incident occurred last Wednesday night, when Lance Corporal Thierry Rodger Pendy, 26, had his right hand severed in a machete attack by a foreign national at an apartment complex in Desa Aman Puri, Kepong.
The suspect, later identified as a Nigerian national, was armed with two machetes and had earlier attacked police officers, firefighters and Health Ministry personnel.
He was later shot dead by police at a nearby playground following a brief chase.

Title: PAS accuses Malaysiakini of taking Hadi’s remarks out of context, rejects racial narrative
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — PAS has accused
Malaysiakini
of publishing a misleading report on its president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang’s remarks, claiming they were taken out of context.
In a statement posted on Hadi’s Facebook page today, the PAS president’s office expressed regret over the report titled “
Sejahat-jahat orang Islam tak sezalim bukan Islam
” (Even the worst Muslim is not as cruel as a non-Muslim), saying it misrepresented the context of Hadi’s speech.
It said Hadi had been explaining that Islamic politics was guided by considerations of sin and reward, which, in turn, would lead to just governance and guarantee the rights of non-Muslims.
“We regret the media narrative, which could cause misunderstandings among the public, and reject any attempt to stir up racial sentiments ahead of polling day for the Melaka state election,” the statement said.

Title: Former Perlis MB Azlan Man faces Jan 20, 2027 decision in RM1.18m false claims trial
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The Sessions Court here will decide on Jan 20 whether former Perlis Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Azlan Man will be called to enter his defence or acquitted of 10 charges involving alleged false claims and receiving proceeds of illegal activities.
Judge Azura Alwi fixed the date after hearing submissions from the prosecution and defence at the end of the prosecution’s case.
The court also set Feb 10 to 12, March 26, and April 16 and 30, 2027, as trial dates should Azlan be ordered to enter his defence.
Earlier, Deputy Public Prosecutor Noralis Mat submitted that Azlan had made five claims for overseas travel facilities between 2013 and 2017, purportedly in his capacity as Menteri Besar, although investigations found that the trips did not take place on the stated dates.
“The 18th prosecution witness (SP18), former Senior Private Secretary to Azlan, Herwardy Hashim, testified that he was instructed by the accused to provide his bank account number to SP10, former managing director of Sri Kedawang Travel & Tour (W) Sdn Bhd (SKTT), Shafiei Ismail, for the purpose of depositing money received by SKTT into the accused’s account.
“This was because the accused wanted to cancel the trip that had been approved through a local order (LO) and undertake the trip himself,” he said.
Noralis said the testimony of the 17th prosecution witness, former Assistant Accountant at the Management Services Division of the Perlis State Secretary’s Office, Mohd Aswad Abdul Razak, established that claims for overseas holiday travel facilities could not be converted into cash.
He said the allocation was intended to cover overseas travel expenses, while payment to the travel agent had already been confirmed by the Menteri Besar’s Office.
He added that this was supported by the testimony of SP12, Perlis Treasury representative Azmi Abdul Latif, who said Azlan could not receive reimbursement for overseas holiday travel claims that had already been made between 2013 and 2017.
“If the holiday trip is cancelled, the travel agent is responsible for cancelling the local order issued to them,” he said.
Noralis further argued that Azlan’s alleged practice of having the money transferred into his personal account every year could not be dismissed as an innocent mistake.
“If the trip is cancelled, the money should have been returned to the Perlis State Government, not handed over to the accused,” he said.
Meanwhile, defence counsel Burhanudeen Abdul Wahid said the Perlis government allocated annual funds to the Menteri Besar for overseas travel, and the services of a travel agent were required to make the necessary bookings and secure the allocation.
He maintained that the entire claims process had been conducted transparently.
“The prosecution claimed that he did not travel but submitted claims for the trips. However, the investigating officer testified that the accused had travelled on other dates,” he said.
Burhanudeen added that the defence had also submitted passport and immigration records to support its position.
Azlan, 67, is facing five charges of submitting false claims involving overseas holiday travel facilities amounting to more than RM1.18 million, allegedly committed at the Perlis State Secretary’s Office between December 2013 and December 2017.
The claims involved flight ticket quotations to London, United Kingdom, as well as invoices issued by SKTT and Aidil Travel & Tours Sdn Bhd.
He is also facing five charges of receiving proceeds of illegal activities amounting to RM1.06 million between Feb 19, 2014 and December 2017 at several locations, including the Maybank branch in Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman, the CIMB Bank branch in Putrajaya and the Sheraton Imperial Hotel here.
In addition, Azlan faces five alternative charges of misappropriating RM1.06 million belonging to the Perlis government, which had been paid to SKTT and Aidil Travel & Tours Sdn Bhd. — Bernama

Title: Anwar raps agencies over repeated flooding in Selangor, orders immediate action
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today criticised government agencies for failing to address flooding in Selangor, calling it unacceptable that residents are forced to endure flooding four to five times a year.
Speaking to reporters after performing Friday prayers in Brickfields here, Anwar said repeated disruptions continue to place a heavy burden on the public, even if floodwaters do not reach high levels.
“Following my engagement with Cabinet ministers and the Selangor state government yesterday, I convened a meeting in Parliament to address the ongoing flood crisis,” he said.
“I cannot accept a situation where residents have to deal with floods four to five times a year. Even if the water levels are not high, the impact still burdens the people.”
Anwar said he had ordered the relevant agencies, including the Department of Irrigation and Drainage, to start mitigation efforts immediately without delaying previously agreed-upon works.
He acknowledged that floods could be caused by factors beyond human control, but stressed that proactive measures must be taken to reduce flood risks and minimise their impact on local communities.
Under Budget 2026, tabled in October 2025, the Anwar administration allocated RM2.2 billion specifically for flood mitigation projects.
Last Monday, Anwar said he had increased cash assistance for flood victims from RM1,000 to RM2,500, while the Selangor state government’s contribution was also increased from RM500 to RM3,000.

Title: Anwar plays down Cabinet tensions, says ‘no need to rush’ on Loke’s resignation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today described the mood at this morning’s Cabinet meeting as “normal”, amid signs of disunity within the government as his Pakatan Harapan coalition goes head-to-head with its unity government ally, Barisan Nasional, in tomorrow’s Melaka state polls.
Anwar played down the tension in the run-up to tomorrow’s vote as part and parcel of an election campaign, and said he anticipates the temperature to cool down again once the election is done.
“When there is an election, the temperature rises briefly. Then it goes back down. But as for the meeting earlier, it was normal. I didn’t notice any issues,” Anwar told reporters after performing Friday prayers at Brickfields here.
Media reports suggested there is growing friction within Anwar’s Cabinet, as the two major governing coalitions traded salvos at the Melaka election campaign trail where incumbent BN had teamed up with rivals Perikatan Nasional to defend the state.
One of Anwar’s staunchest backers, Anthony Loke, has also resigned as transport minister in what is seen as a protest against the conditional royal clemency granted to Datuk Seri Mohd Najib Razak, allowing the former prime minister to serve the remainder of his jail sentence for his SRC International corruption convictions at home.
Anwar said he has yet to decide whether to accept Loke’s resignation and was in no rush to do so.
“I have not accepted the resignation yet. I have received the letter and he said it takes effect (immediately), but I will certainly take some time to review it carefully,” he told reporters.
“There is no need for us to rush.”

Title: N. Sembilan police begin deployment of 261 personnel for Melaka election
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 13 — A total of 261 police officers and personnel from Negeri Sembilan have been deployed to help ensure smooth and orderly polling in the 16th Melaka State Election tomorrow.
Negeri Sembilan Police Chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the deployment began yesterday to facilitate early preparations for polling.
“Logistical arrangements and personnel movements in Melaka will be subject to the directives and operational requirements there.
“We will extend the necessary cooperation to help ensure public safety and order throughout the election process,” he told Bernama here today.
The Election Commission (EC) said 675,166 ordinary voters are eligible to cast their ballots tomorrow, with turnout expected to reach 70 per cent. — Bernama

Title: High Court dismisses application to remove administrators of Genting heiress’ RM1.6b estate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The High Court here today dismissed an application by the son of the late Genting heiress Lim Siew Kim to remove two interim administrators overseeing the RM1.6 billion estate.
Judge Datuk Mahazan Mat Taib dismissed Marcus Chan Jau Chwen’s application against lawyer Datuk S. Satharuban and Khoo Siew Kiat and ordered him to pay RM30,000 in costs to the two administrators.
The court also discharged the interim injunction restraining the two from acting as administrators of the estate, allowing them to resume their duties under the court’s supervision.
In her ruling, Mahzan said Marcus had failed to establish misconduct, persistent breaches of duty, a disqualifying conflict of interest or other sufficiently serious circumstances to justify their removal.
“I find that Marcus has failed to establish sufficient grounds for the removal of the joint administrators pendente lite. However, dismissing the application does not amount to blanket approval of every expenditure or transaction undertaken by the administrators.
“Their obligations to account for estate assets, comply with the appointment order and submit their costs and remuneration for examination remain unaffected,” she said.
On allegations of interference in companies linked to the estate, Mahazan said the administrators could not classify the companies’ liabilities as debts of the estate simply on the basis that Siew Kim held shares in those entities.
However, she said they remained responsible for safeguarding the estate’s interests, which could include obtaining relevant information and taking lawful action to protect the value of its shareholdings.
The judge also ruled that the evidence was insufficient to establish unlawful interference in the companies’ affairs or misuse of estate funds warranting the administrators’ removal.
She clarified that the decision did not address the validity of Siew Kim’s will or determine the beneficiaries’ entitlements.
Siew Kim, who died of cancer in July 2022 at the age of 73, left behind three daughters and a son. Her estate has since been administered by interim administrators amid an ongoing family dispute over the validity of her will.
On November 27, 2023, the High Court appointed Satharuban Sivasubramaniam and Khoo as administrators pendente lite to oversee the estate.
Their appointment followed a probate suit filed by two of Siew Kim’s daughters, Chan T’shiao Li and Kimberly Chan T’shiao Miin, on January 19, 2023, challenging the validity of a will said to have been executed on April 28, 2022.
Marcus, Siew Kim’s only son and a 30 per cent beneficiary of the residuary estate, sought the removal of both administrators, alleging misconduct and non-compliance with the court order governing their appointment.
Among his complaints were allegations that certain payments had been made to solicitors and other parties through individual bank accounts instead of consolidated trust accounts, resulting in the wrongful depletion of estate funds.
He also accused the administrators of interfering in the management of companies linked to the estate.
Marcus further alleged that the administrators had nearly caused the estate to pay RM4.73 million in assessments on behalf of Prominview Sdn Bhd, although the liability allegedly rested with a joint-venture partner.
Other complaints included the lodging of private caveats and the commissioning of property valuations despite the administrators allegedly having no authority to distribute or dispose of estate assets.
On January 23, 2026, Marcus obtained an ad interim injunction restraining the administrators from acting on behalf of the estate pending the disposal of his application to remove them. — Bernama

Title: ‘The next move is yours’: Umno tells DAP to talk, not threaten, amid Najib pardon row
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Umno has urged DAP to resolve its differences with coalition partners through dialogue and consultation, instead of issuing public ultimatums or demanding resignations, following the controversy over Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional pardon.
Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said, described DAP chairman Gobind Singh Deo’s call for Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi to resign if he did not support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s leadership, as regrettable and unhelpful to the unity government’s stability.
“Issuing public ultimatums to the president of a coalition partner is neither constructive nor consistent with the spirit of the Coalition Agreement,” she said in a statement today.
Azalina, who is also Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), said the agreement did not require coalition partners to agree unconditionally with every political position taken by the prime minister or other political leaders.
She outlined four options for DAP, including invoking the agreement’s mediation mechanism, allowing existing arrangements to continue or seeking a review of the agreement.
She said terminating it would ultimately point towards the dissolution of Parliament, as it contained no provision for termination before the end of the 15th Parliament.
On Najib’s conditional pardon, Azalina said the exercise of the royal prerogative of mercy under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution should not be portrayed as a unilateral political decision by any party.
She also defended Umno’s continued participation in the unity government, saying the party would honour its commitments, respect Anwar’s leadership and uphold the Federal Constitution.
“We have made our position clear. The next move is yours,” she said.

Title: Cops await DPP instructions for 15 more cases of impersonating Selangor Raja Muda’s aide-de-camp
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 13 — The police are awaiting instructions from the office of the Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) regarding 15 more cases of individuals impersonating the aide-de-camp (ADC) of the Raja Muda of Selangor in vehicle and property transactions.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said that 17 investigation papers have been opened based on the police reports received, and all of them have been completed before being referred to the Selangor DPP office for further instructions.
“Yesterday and today, the DPP agreed to charge a male and female suspect in court under Section 109 and Section 420 of the Penal Code.
“As for the other 15 cases, the police are waiting for feedback from the DPP’s office for any further instructions,” he said at the Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) media conference at the Selangor police contingent headquarters (IPK) here today.
Earlier, the media reported that Al Zulfadly Alias, 40, pleaded guilty while another accused, Nurul Nur Syahirah Kamarudin, 37, pleaded not guilty at the Klang Magistrate’s Court on charges of fraud involving the sale of an auctioned vehicle worth RM40,000 in April.
Yesterday, both the accused recorded their pleas at the Shah Alam Magistrate’s Court regarding the charge of fraud involving the sale of an auctioned vehicle worth RM30,000 in May.
The police had previously confirmed the arrest of a man believed to be the main suspect in a vehicle and residential sales fraud case using the image of the Raja Muda of Selangor around Johor Bahru on October 27.
Commenting further, Shazeli said the investigation found nearly 27 cases reported nationwide, including 17 in Selangor, with estimated losses amounting to RM1.4 million.
He also expressed appreciation to the public who came forward to cooperate in providing information until the suspect was brought to justice and advised the public to be vigilant to avoid becoming victims of fraud.
Meanwhile, Shazeli said his team also successfully dismantled two online fraud syndicates or ‘call centres’ with the arrest of 11 individuals in two operations in Sungai Long, Kajang and Taman Aman Perdana on November 3 and 10 respectively.
“The syndicate, which has been operating since September, targets foreigners living abroad as victims by offering them investment schemes and ‘love scams’.
“All the suspects, including 10 foreign nationals, aged 22 to 45, acted as customer service operators. The police also seized various equipment worth RM20,000,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Rosmah’s defamation suit: Nov 24 hearing for Harith Iskander’s lawyers to discharge themselves
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The High Court here today fixed November 24 to hear an application by lawyers Sangeet Kaur Deo and Harkiranjit Kaur Manjit Singh to discharge themselves from representing comedian and actor Harith Iskander in a defamation suit filed by Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor.
“Yes, we have applied to discharge ourselves from representing (Harith Iskander),” Sangeet confirmed when contacted.
The case management proceedings for the application were held online today before Judge Arziah Mohamed Apandi, with Sangeet and Harkiranjit attending alongside Rosmah’s lawyers, Mohamed Baharudeen Mohamed Ariff and Nur-Diana Ezlyn Hashim.
Meanwhile, Mohamed Baharudeen told reporters that the hearing of the application on November 24 would be conducted online via Zoom at 2.15pm.
Rosmah, 74, filed a defamation suit through Messrs Hafarizam & Aisha Mubarak against Harith Iskander Musa, 60, on June 9, claiming he insulted and body-shamed her during his stand-up comedy performance, Harith Iskander: The Outspoken Comedy Tour, at a hotel in Melaka on January 17.
The former Prime Minister’s wife claimed in her statement of claim that the defendant had shown an image of frightening mythical creatures before displaying her image, followed by remarks mocking the idea of looking in the rear-view mirror while driving along a dark road.
Rosmah also alleged that a TikTok user uploaded a recording of the performance, which garnered hundreds of thousands of views and damaged her reputation and dignity as a public figure and patron of charitable organisations.
In the suit, she is seeking general, aggravated, and exemplary damages; an injunction to prevent the statements from being republished; and a written apology in two mainstream newspapers and on social media accounts.
However, in his statement of defence filed on July 9, Harith Iskander denied that the image was defamatory, adding that the TikTok clip was published without his knowledge or consent and did not reflect the full context of the comedy performance. — Bernama

Title: IRB’s RM1.69b appeal in Najib bankruptcy case set for Feb 23; no appeal for Nazifuddin
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 13 — The Federal Court has fixed February 23 next year to hear the Inland Revenue Board’s (IRB) application for leave to appeal against the Court of Appeal’s decision granting former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak a stay of bankruptcy proceedings against him.
Lawyer Wee Yeong Kang, representing Najib, confirmed the hearing date to Bernama when contacted.
He said the date was fixed during an earlier case management session early this month (November 4).
A further case management session was held today before Federal Court Deputy Registrar Norshakinah Ahmad Kamarudin.
Wee also confirmed that the IRB had not filed an application for leave to appeal against the Court of Appeal’s decision granting a stay of bankruptcy proceedings against Najib’s son, Datuk Mohd Nazifuddin.
On September 4, the Court of Appeal ruled in favour of Najib and Mohd Nazifuddin, allowing their applications to stay the bankruptcy proceedings pending the disposal of their appeals before the Special Commissioners of Income Tax (SCIT) over additional tax assessments issued by the IRB.
A three-member panel chaired by Justice Datuk Dr Alwi Abdul Wahab ruled that the stay was warranted as both appellants had raised specific issues that required determination by the SCIT.
Justice Alwi said there were substantial issues concerning alleged errors in the computation of the taxable amount of approximately RM1.69 billion, including claims of double taxation and the treatment of refunded donations and dividends used for charitable and political purposes.
He noted that the IRB had not disputed the merits of these issues, maintaining instead that they should be properly determined by the SCIT.
The bankruptcy proceedings stemmed from separate High Court decisions granting the IRB’s applications for summary judgment against Najib and his son over unpaid income tax arrears for the 2011 to 2017 assessment years.
The IRB is seeking to recover RM1.69 billion from Najib and RM37.6 million from Mohd Nazifuddin.
Both Najib and Mohd Nazifuddin had previously failed in their appeals before the Court of Appeal and Federal Court to set aside the summary judgments.
Following this, bankruptcy notices were issued against them. They subsequently applied for a stay of the bankruptcy proceedings, but their applications were dismissed by High Court Deputy Registrar Kamarul Aris Kamalluddin on July 29, 2024.
Their subsequent appeals to the High Court were also unsuccessful, prompting them to take the matter to the Court of Appeal, which eventually ruled in their favour.
Najib is currently serving the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest at his residence in Kuala Lumpur, following payment of the RM50 million fine.
In September this year, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, granted Najib a further conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and compliance with other stipulated conditions. — Bernama

Title: Survey: BN-Perikatan poised to dominate in Melaka as Pakatan-Bersatu grassroots synergy sputters
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Backchannel political cooperation has not generated grassroots synergy for Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Bersatu in the Melaka state election, leaving an openly coordinated Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional (BN-PN) pact on course to claim up to 24 seats, according to think tank Ilham Centre.
In a pre-polling study released on the eve of the vote, the research outfit found that the federal Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) between the Madani administration and Bersatu showed “little evidence of effectiveness” in forging voter-level alignment.
The firm noted that the arrangements conducted without open public messaging have alienated fence-sitters and left party loyalists adhering to traditional rivalries rather than pooling their votes.
The disconnect contrasts sharply with the formalised coordination achieved by BN and PN, which has synchronized grassroots campaign machinery and produced high vote transferability.
According to Ilham’s findings, 91 per cent of PN supporters expressed readiness to vote for BN candidates, while 78 per cent of BN voters were willing to back PN contenders. Under their shared electoral slate, BN is contesting 23 of Melaka’s 28 seats, with PN fielding candidates in the remaining five.
Ilham cautioned that in a first-past-the-post electoral system, vote splitting between parties sharing common political space provides an overwhelming structural advantage to unified opponents.
“PH and Bersatu must demonstrate greater political resolve in formalising an electoral alliance,” the firm said, warning that without formal agreements on candidate slates, seat quotas, common narratives, and integrated machinery, the partnership remains trapped as an “elite-level understanding”.
Based on stated voter preferences, Ilham projects the BN-PN alliance to lead in 24 constituencies, building upon the decisive majority BN secured in the 2021 state election when it claimed 21 seats.
Conversely, PH appears safe in only two urban strongholds, Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir, while its defensive battles in Ayer Keroh and Kesidang remain too close to call.
The report characterised PH’s support as “stable but stagnant”, noting that its appeal remains locked within non-Malay and urban precincts with negligible traction among Malay, rural, and undecided voters.
The survey gathered responses from 805 registered voters across all 28 constituencies between Nov 1 and 12 through stratified random sampling, supported by five focus group discussions and 22 in-depth interviews.
Carrying a statewide margin of error of 3.45 percentage points at a 95 per cent confidence level, the survey measures declared voting intent ahead of polling day tomorrow, Nov 14, following early voting on Nov 10.

Title: Zero cases of overpricing under Deepavali 2026 festive price control scheme, Domestic Trade Ministry reports
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 13 — The Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) recorded zero cases of sales exceeding the maximum price during the implementation of the Deepavali 2026 Festive Season Maximum Price Scheme (SHMMP) from November 4-10.
KPDN Enforcement director-general Datuk Azman Adam said the achievement reflected an improvement in trader compliance compared with last year, when six violations involving the sale of goods above the controlled prices were recorded.
“For this year, KPDN did not receive any complaints throughout the scheme’s implementation.
“This is a positive development compared with one complaint received at the retail level last year,” he said in a statement today.
He said that, overall, the number of enforcement cases taken by the KPDN during the implementation of the Deepavali 2026 SHMMP increased to 482, compared with 445 last year.
“Of the total, 481 cases involved the retail sector and one the wholesale sector, compared with 444 retail cases and one wholesale case last year,” he added.
Azman said the total compound value recorded this year decreased to RM50,800 compared with RM53,500 in 2025, while the value of seized goods also declined to RM14,045 from RM16,078 the previous year.
He said the majority of the offences detected involved traders failing to display the special pink price tags, with 481 cases recorded this year compared with 433 in 2025.
As for offences involving failure to display price tags, there was a significant drop as only one case was recorded compared to six last year.
“KPDN would like to express its appreciation to all parties involved throughout the implementation of the SHMMP this year, which resulted in zero cases of offences involving the sale of goods above the stipulated maximum prices,” he added. — Bernama

Title: ‘Corruption is corruption’: Saifuddin takes aim at Hadi over remarks on Muslim, non-Muslim leaders
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Nov 13 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has criticised PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang over his remarks that even the worst Muslim government is less oppressive than a non-Muslim administration, saying leaders should be judged by their integrity and actions, not religion.
In a statement today, Saifuddin Nasution said such comparisons were regrettable as they risked using religion to divide society and excuse wrongdoing by political leaders.
He said Islam taught Muslims to uphold justice even towards those they disliked, citing verse eight of Surah Al-Maidah, which states: “Do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just, for that is closer to righteousness.”
Saifuddin Nasution questioned the suggestion that an oppressive Muslim leader should be considered better than a non-Muslim simply because of their religious identity.
He said a leader’s worth should instead be measured by their trustworthiness, fairness and ability to protect the people under their care.
“Corruption is corruption. Oppression is oppression. Betrayal of trust remains wrongdoing, regardless of who commits it.
“We must not use religion to provide moral protection for corrupt leaders,” he said.
He stressed that Islam’s standing should not be built by belittling other religions.
Saifuddin stressed that Islam’s standing should not be elevated by belittling other religions, adding that respecting the rights of other races and faiths would not weaken the Malay community or Muslims.
Instead, he said Muslims would earn greater respect by setting an example through justice, progress, wisdom and compassion towards all people.
He also said elections should not become platforms for stirring racial and religious fears or prejudice.
His statement followed Hadi’s remarks at the Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional grand finale rally in Melaka, where the PAS president urged Muslims to vote, warning that their failure to do so could allow non-Muslims to take power.

Title: Police foil attempt to smuggle over 9kg of syabu worth RM476,180 to Indonesia via Port Dickson jetty
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 13 — Negeri Sembilan police foiled an attempt to smuggle 9.238 kilogrammes (kg) of drugs believed to be syabu (methamphetamine), worth RM476,180, to Indonesia at the Port Dickson Passenger Jetty Terminal here two days ago.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said an Indonesian man, in his 20s and believed to be a drug mule, was also arrested after he was spotted acting suspiciously while carrying a medium-sized black suitcase at the terminal at about 9.30am.
He said that upon inspecting the suitcase, police found a modified compartment used to conceal six packages containing about five kg of drugs believed to be syabu, along with clothing.
“Following the arrest, we conducted a further search at a condominium in Cheras, Kuala Lumpur, where the suspect had been staying since arriving in the country on November 4, and found another piece of luggage containing the same type of drugs, weighing about 4.238kg.
“The suspect is a recent graduate in Islamic Studies and Arabic Language from a higher education institution in Aceh, and had come to Malaysia in search of employment. At the time of his arrest, he was believed to be en route to Tanjung Balai, Indonesia,” he told a media conference here today.
Alzafny said investigations found that the suspect was believed to have entered Malaysia for the first time, based on the entry stamp in his passport, and was suspected of having been contacted by another Indonesian man in Malaysia before being offered a job to transport drugs back to his home country.
He said the suspect was promised a payment of 30 million rupiah (about RM6,777) for every successful drug delivery.
“He was given a choice of either working at an eatery or restaurant, or taking the risk of transporting drugs to Indonesia. He tested negative for drugs and has no previous criminal record,” he added.
He said police believed that the suspect might have returned to Malaysia to collect another piece of luggage for a subsequent delivery, had the first attempt been successful.
Alzafny said police are intensifying efforts to track down the other Indonesian man, believed to be the supplier of the drugs, who is still in Malaysia.
He said the operation was carried out based on intelligence gathering and cooperationn with the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM), after receiving information about drug smuggling activities via sea routes from Malaysia to Indonesia.
“Following the information received, I instructed the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) to conduct surveillance whenever ferries operated at the terminal, which provides ferry services to Dumai and Tanjung Balai in Indonesia, with two return trips daily,” he added.
He said police also did not rule out the possibility that the sea route was being used by syndicates to smuggle drugs into Indonesia for the country’s market.
The case is being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952. — Bernama
